# Golden files

Each file is `{ "ruleset": "<fixture name>", "input": Input, "output": Output }` and is decoded with the contract's shape rules (unknown or missing members and `null` fail). `ruleset` names a file in `../rulesets/`.

**The expected `output` is written by hand from the spec (SAD §5.1–§5.3, spec F05 and F13.2) before the engine code exists.** A changed expectation is re-derived by hand here first. An expectation is never written from engine output.

`TestGolden` compares compact bytes, so it enforces the canonical encoding: members of `output` in Go struct order (`ruleSetVersion`, `today`, `assessments`; `disease`, `bucket` or `block`, `nextDose`, `seriesUsed`, `products`, `estimated`, `reasons`; `number`, `earliest`, `due`, `overdue`; `code`, `params`; `product`, `series` in a `candidates` element), `params` keys sorted, optional members omitted when empty. It decodes the expectation into an Output and re-encodes it to tell the cases apart:

- the expectation does not decode (an unknown, renamed, missing or `null` member, a wrong type, a bad date), or writes an optional member with an empty or zero value (`"series": ""`, `"number": 0`, `"params": {}`): an error, never rewritten;
- the same values in a different encoding (member order, spacing): fails with a hint; `go test ./engine -run TestGolden -update` rewrites the `output` member with the canonical encoding of the expectation itself;
- different values: fails with "re-derive by hand"; `-update` never writes it.

**A contract migration is its own commit.** It changes the Go types, the schema and the fixture/golden files (by hand or with an uncommitted script) and no decision logic, with one carve-out: a migration that adds an output member may add the code that emits it, and changes no other decoded value (issue #14, S3a's `seriesUsed`). The otherwise unchanged engine then checks the migrated files byte for byte.

## Notation

- E = earliest allowed date, Du = due date, O = overdue date.
- Per plan: E = max(birth + minAge, latest dose in time + minInterval); Du = max(E, anchor + offset); O = max(Du + buffer, Du + 7d).
- Alternative plans: E and Du from the plan with the smallest Du (SAD §5.3 step 7 merge 1, A7), even when another plan has a smaller E; O = the latest O of all plans. Plans with the same Du: E is the latest of theirs (P1, SAD §5.3 step 7 merge 1).
- T30 = today + 30 days; T6m = today + 6 months (always added to today).
- Bucket: today ≥ O → overdue; else today ≥ E and Du ≤ T30 → due; else Du ≤ T6m → upcoming; else ≥ 1 dose counted → complete + `ON_TRACK`; else `notYetScheduled`. `DOSE_INVALID` → unknown with no nextDose; the reasons of the masked bucket (`COMPLETE`, `ON_TRACK`, `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`; since S3a also `PRODUCT_NOT_IN_CATALOG`, and `SAFEST_SERIES` when no dose is given, see the S3a notation) stay (SAD §5.3 step 10). A record-scoped date problem (`INVALID_DATE`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `DATE_IN_FUTURE`, `DATE_BEFORE_BIRTH`) on any record of the disease → unknown with no nextDose and one reason per such record, sorted by record ID: the doses are not walked (SAD §5.3 steps 2–9 are skipped), so there is no `DOSE_INVALID`, `COMPLETE`, `ON_TRACK` or `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS` (SAD §5.1, §5.3 step 1). These are the only reasons because S1 has no precedence layer above data ⚪; a later slice's layers 1–5 win over it and keep the record reasons as masked reasons (SAD §5.3 step 10).
- Months keep the day of month and clamp to the month end; 1w = 7d; 1y = 12m. In the S1 derivations every date is precision `day`; the S2 notation below covers the other precisions.
- Fixtures write spans as ISO 8601 durations with one designator (`"P6W"`, `"P2M"`, `"P14D"`); the derivations below write them short (6w, 2m, 14d).

### S2 notation (imprecise dates, dose positions, two birth ends, no birth date)

- Inputs: `m` = precision `month` (value `YYYY-MM`), `y` = precision `year` (value `YYYY`), `U` = precision `unknown` (level 4, no value), `#n` = `doseNumbers {disease: n}`, birth `none` = no birth date (no value). `est` = `"estimated": true`; an assessment without `est` omits the member.
- A dose range is R = [Lo, Hi] = [period start, min(period end, today)] (EQ7). The birth range is [b_lo, b_hi] with b_hi = min(period end, today) (EQ17). A day-precise date is a one-day range.
- Record date problems use the ranges (step 1, issue #13). A dose is `DATE_IN_FUTURE` only when its whole period is after today (period start > today). It is `DATE_BEFORE_BIRTH` only when its whole range is before the whole birth range (R.Hi < b_lo). A partial overlap is not a problem: the dose is walked and checked at each birth end like any other dose. At a birth end later than the dose, the dose gets no special treatment: a positive minimum age makes it definitely invalid there (R.Hi < b + minAge).
- Dose checks at one birth end (SAD §5.3 step 5, F05.10). Minimum age: definite if R.Hi < b + minAge, possible if R.Lo < b + minAge. Minimum interval to a dated predecessor P in time: definite if R.Hi < P.Lo + minInterval, possible if R.Lo < P.Hi + minInterval. `minIntervalFromFirst` likewise against dose 1: its range when dose 1 is dated, and the earliest dates of the chain below (best and worst end) when dose 1 is level 4 or implied. A dose passes when some plan passes all its checks (A7). Definite under every plan → `DOSE_INVALID{checks, dose, number}`, not counted. Otherwise, possible under every plan → `DOSE_POSSIBLY_INVALID{checks, dose, number}`, counted. `checks` are listed in catalog order: `minAge`, `minInterval`, `minIntervalFromFirst`.
- Undated predecessor (level 4 or implied, EQ8, EQ20b): the interval to it is waived and the dose is counted with `INTERVAL_UNVERIFIABLE{dose, number}`. Feasibility: each undated position q takes its earliest date, max(previous + minInterval_q, b + minAge_q, dose 1 + `minIntervalFromFirst`_q) under the most lenient plan, starting from the dated dose before the run (or from the birth date). A dated dose after the run must be ≥ that chain end + its own minInterval; when it is not, even at the best end of the ranges, it is `DOSE_INVALID{checks: [minInterval]}`. A dated dose beyond the series length is not checked itself, but the run before it must fit on or before it (chain end ≤ its R.Hi), or it is `DOSE_INVALID{checks: [minInterval]}`, with its position. Undated doses after the last dated dose must fit by today: the last one is checked as if given today, with the checks that fail; when it is implied, the level-4 record beyond the series whose number implies it carries the reason, with that number. Unnumbered level-4 records that fill no gap (as many as the series still needs, the last ones by ID) must have some placement among the dated doses that adds no `DOSE_INVALID`: each in front of a counted dated dose with no number and no numbered dated dose after it (moving it and the later doses up one position), or after every dose. When every such placement fits only at one end of the ranges, the first one tried (all after the last dated dose, then the earliest insertion points first) adds its new `DOSE_POSSIBLY_INVALID` reasons and every dose stays counted. When none fits, the last of them by ID is `DOSE_INVALID{checks, dose, number}`, not counted, with the position and checks it fails when they all go after the last dated dose (checked as if given today).
- Positions (SAD §5.3 step 2, F04.1, F04.2). Two dated ranges overlap when they intersect and are not both single days; exact doses on the same day have no time order between them: when some have numbers, those sit at their numbers and the unnumbered ones take the free positions after the position reached before that day, by ID, and the day is walked in position order (without numbers, they keep the S1 order by ID). An overlap is resolved only when every dose in it has a number; otherwise it is ⚪ `OVERLAPPING_ESTIMATED_DATES{doses}`, with the record IDs in time order. A duplicate number, or a number not above the running position counter, is ⚪ `NUMBERING_CONFLICT{dose, number}` on the later record. Gaps below the highest position are filled first by unnumbered level-4 records (by ID); the remaining gaps are implied doses, `IMPLIED_EARLIER_DOSES{numbers}`. An unnumbered level-4 record that fills no gap has no position and may be the latest dose. A ⚪ from step 2 skips steps 5–9, as a step-1 ⚪ does.
- Next dose k (SAD §5.3 step 7). E = max(b_hi + minAge, latest dated dose in time R.Hi + minInterval, dose 1 R.Hi + `minIntervalFromFirst`); `firstDose` and `previousDose` anchors use R.Hi too. ⚪ `PREVIOUS_DOSE_DATE_UNKNOWN{dose}` applies when dose k−1 is undated or an unnumbered level-4 record may be the latest dose; it stops step 7, so no `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`, `ON_TRACK` or `FIRST_DOSE_DATE_ASSUMED` is added. Dose k−1 is the counted dose at position k−1. An uncounted (`DOSE_INVALID`) dated dose walked after it does not change that: the earliest date is not measured from the uncounted dose while dose k−1 is undated. If dose 1 is undated and a rule uses the first dose, the earliest dated dose stands in for it: `FIRST_DOSE_DATE_ASSUMED{dose}` (EQ20c).
- Two birth ends (SAD §5.3 step 4, F05.5). Steps 5–9 run at b_lo and at b_hi. The later end's result (with its dates) is used, with `est`, when the ends agree on the visible class, the next dose number and the blocking reasons. Dates alone never make the ends differ: SAD §5.3 step 4 and F05.5 take the dates driven by a minimum age or interval from the later end, which only means something when two results with different dates count as the same result. So two 🔴 ends, or two 🟠 ends, with different dates give the later end's 🔴 or 🟠. It is also used when both classes are in {`notYetScheduled`, upcoming, complete + `ON_TRACK`}. Any other difference gives ⚪ `BIRTH_DATE_IMPRECISE{hint}`, with hint `birthMonth` for a year-precision birth and `fullBirthDate` for a month-precision birth. Its reasons are `BIRTH_DATE_IMPRECISE`, then the later end's reasons, then the older end's reasons that are not already listed (A8).
- No birth date (EQ19). No minimum-age check. A birth-anchored due date for dose k is max(E, last counted dose + (offset_k − offset_{k−1})). The result is ⚪ `NO_BIRTH_DATE` when no dose is counted, or when dose k's minimum age is not implied (minAge_k ≤ minAge_1 + Σ minInterval of doses 2…k, SAD §5.2).
- Blocking reasons make the assessment ⚪, with no nextDose. Informational reasons (`IMPLIED_EARLIER_DOSES`, `INTERVAL_UNVERIFIABLE`, `FIRST_DOSE_DATE_ASSUMED`) never do so on their own. Reason order:
  1. `IMPLIED_EARLIER_DOSES`;
  2. `BIRTH_DATE_IMPRECISE`;
  3. per dose, in walk order, `DOSE_INVALID`, `DOSE_POSSIBLY_INVALID` or `INTERVAL_UNVERIFIABLE`;
  4. `COMPLETE`;
  5. `PREVIOUS_DOSE_DATE_UNKNOWN`;
  6. `NO_BIRTH_DATE`;
  7. `FIRST_DOSE_DATE_ASSUMED`;
  8. `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`;
  9. `ON_TRACK`.
- `estimated` (SAD §5.3 step 1) is set on every assessment, ⚪ included, when the birth date is not day-precise, when any dose record of the disease is not day-precise (`unknown` included), or when the disease has an implied dose.
- `illustrative-vn` (version `illustrative-vn-s2`) adds `hpv`: dose 1 min age 9y at birth + 9y; dose 2 min interval 4w at `firstDose` + 2m; dose 3 min interval 12w, `minIntervalFromFirst` 5m, at `firstDose` + 6m. In the S2 derivations, "pertussis and measles overdue (b 2010-05-20)" means: pertussis overdue {1, 2010-07-01, 2010-07-20, 2010-07-27} with `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS{series: pertussis-primary}` (E = b + 42d, Du = b + 2m in both plans); measles overdue {1, 2011-02-20, 2011-02-20, 2011-02-27}. Also, "hpv notYetScheduled" means: no hpv dose, E = Du = b + 9y > T6m, O = Du + 7d.

## Derivations

### illustrative-vn

These files were written against version `illustrative-vn-s1`. S2 changed the fixture to version `illustrative-vn-s2` and added the `hpv` disease (issue #13, a decided contract addition), so each file now names `illustrative-vn-s2` and ends with an `hpv` assessment, derived by hand like the rest. None of these inputs has an `hpv` record, and every birth date is day-precise, so `hpv` is "hpv notYetScheduled" as defined in the S2 notation (E = Du = b + 9y > T6m, O = Du + 7d, not est). That gives {1, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-17} for birth 2026-01-10, {1, 2034-01-15, 2034-01-15, 2034-01-22} for birth 2025-01-15 and {1, 2035-03-01, 2035-03-01, 2035-03-08} for birth 2026-03-01. The latest today among these files is 2026-05-17, so T6m is at most 2026-11-17, well before those due dates.

- `f13-5-week-old-upcoming`: birth 2026-01-10, today 2026-02-14 (5 weeks old), no doses. Pertussis dose 1 in both plans: E = 01-10 + 42d = 02-21; Du = max(02-21, 01-10 + 2m = 03-10) = 03-10; O = 03-17. T30 = 03-16; today < E and Du ≤ T30 → upcoming, `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`. Measles: E = Du = 01-10 + 9m = 10-10, O = 10-17; T6m = 08-14 < Du, no dose → `notYetScheduled`. hpv notYetScheduled {1, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-17}.
- `f13-no-dose-not-yet-scheduled`: birth = today = 2026-03-01. Pertussis: E = 03-01 + 42d = 04-12, Du = 05-01, O = 05-08; T30 = 03-31 < Du ≤ T6m = 09-01 → upcoming, `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`. Measles: E = Du = 12-01, O = 12-08; Du > T6m = 09-01, no dose → `notYetScheduled`. hpv notYetScheduled {1, 2035-03-01, 2035-03-01, 2035-03-08}.
- `f13-on-track`: birth 2025-01-15, today 2025-11-01. Pertussis p1 03-15 ≥ 01-15 + 42d = 02-26; p2 04-15 ≥ 03-15 + 28d = 04-12; p3 05-15 ≥ 04-15 + 28d = 05-13: 3 of 3 counted → complete, `COMPLETE`, no nextDose. Measles m1 2025-10-15 = 01-15 + 9m (inclusive) → counted; dose 2: E = 10-15 + 28d = 11-12, Du = 01-15 + 18m = 2026-07-15, O = 2026-07-22; T6m = 2026-05-01 < Du, 1 dose → complete, `ON_TRACK`. hpv notYetScheduled {1, 2034-01-15, 2034-01-15, 2034-01-22}.
- `alt-plans-due-window`: birth 2026-01-10, p1 03-10 (≥ 02-21, counted), today 04-20. Dose 2: plan 2-3-4 E = 03-10 + 28d = 04-07, Du = 01-10 + 3m = 04-10, O = 04-17; plan 2-4-6 E = 04-07, Du = 05-10, O = 05-17. Measles E = Du = 10-10, O = 10-17; Du ≤ T6m = 10-20 → upcoming. hpv notYetScheduled {1, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-17}.
- `alt-plans-overdue-from-latest-plan`: as above, today 2026-05-17 = merged O → overdue, `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`. Measles Du 10-10 ≤ T6m = 11-17 → upcoming. hpv notYetScheduled {1, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-17}.
- `a9-invalid-date-every-disease-of-record`: r1 value "2026-02-30" (no such day) on pertussis and measles → both unknown, `INVALID_DATE{dose: r1}`, no nextDose. r1 is not an hpv record, so hpv notYetScheduled {1, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-10, 2035-01-17}.

- `f13-dose-before-min-age`: today 02-20, r1 02-14 < 02-21 → `DOSE_INVALID{checks: [minAge], dose: r1, number: 1}`, not counted; no dose counted, so the masked bucket cannot be complete (no `COMPLETE` or `ON_TRACK`) → unknown, `DOSE_INVALID` only, no nextDose.
- `f13-dose-before-min-interval`: today 04-01, r1 03-10 counted; r2 03-31 < 03-10 + 28d = 04-07 → `DOSE_INVALID{checks: [minInterval], dose: r2, number: 2}`. Dose 2: E = r2 03-31 + 28d = 04-28, Du = 05-10, O = 05-17; Du ≤ T6m = 10-01 → the masked bucket is upcoming (no reason) → unknown, `DOSE_INVALID` only, no nextDose. (The earliest date after an uncounted dose, measured from that dose, is pinned by `TestNextAfterUncountedDose`.)
- `a4-interval-to-adjacent-dose`: today 04-15. The input lists the doses out of time order (r3, r1, r2); the engine walks them in time order (SAD §5.3 step 2). r1 03-10 counted. r2 03-24 < 04-07 → invalid. r3 04-14 < r2 03-24 + 28d = 04-21 → invalid (measured to the adjacent r2; against r1 it would pass and complete the series). Dose 2: E = r3 04-14 + 28d = 05-12, Du = max(E, 05-10) = 05-12, O = 05-19; Du ≤ T6m = 10-15 → the masked bucket is upcoming (no reason) → unknown, no nextDose, two `DOSE_INVALID` reasons in dose time order.
- `repeat-dose-1-counted-from-min-age`: today 03-01; r1 02-20 < 02-21 → `DOSE_INVALID{checks: [minAge], dose: r1, number: 1}`, not counted. r2 02-21 is checked for position 1 again: dose 1 has only a minimum age (no minimum interval in the rule model), 02-21 ≥ 02-21 → counted, although it is one day after r1. Dose 2: E = r2 02-21 + 28d = 03-21, Du = max(E, 05-10) = 05-10, O = 05-17; today < E and Du ≤ T6m = 09-01 → the masked bucket is upcoming, which has no reason (complete + `ON_TRACK` would need Du > T6m) → unknown with `DOSE_INVALID` only, no nextDose. (Whether a repeat must be spaced from the invalid dose is open for clinical review, SAD §15.)
- `complete`: today 06-01, r1 03-10 counted, r2 05-10 ≥ 04-07 counted → complete, `COMPLETE`.
- `boundary-dose-on-min-interval-counted`: today 04-10, r1 03-10 counted, r2 04-07 = r1 + 28d exactly → the minimum interval is met on the day it is reached, counted → complete, `COMPLETE`. (An exclusive check would give unknown, `DOSE_INVALID{checks: [minInterval], dose: r2, number: 2}`.)
- `boundary-due-on-earliest-date`: no doses, today 02-21 = E, Du 03-10 ≤ T30 = 03-23, today < O 03-17 → due (the 🟠 condition today ≥ E is inclusive; today 02-20 would be upcoming).
- `f13-buffer0-due-on-due-date`: no doses, today 03-10 = Du: today ≥ E 02-21, Du ≤ T30, today < O 03-17 → due.
- `buffer0-due-day-before-overdue`: today 03-16 < O 03-17 → due.
- `f13-buffer0-overdue-at-due-plus-7`: today 03-17 = Du + 7d = O → overdue.

## S3a derivations (products and candidate series, issue #14)

### S3a notation

- Output members, in order: `disease`, `bucket` or `block`, `nextDose`, `seriesUsed`, `products`, `estimated`, `reasons`. Input dose records: `id`, `diseases`, `product`, `freeProduct`, `date`, `doseNumbers`.
- Inputs: `rotarix`, `hexaxim` and so on = `product` with that catalog ID; `free` = `freeProduct` "Vắc xin khác" ("Other vaccine"); `none` = neither member (an unknown product).
- Candidates (SAD §5.3 step 3, A2, EQ14, F11.3). With doses given, per record: a non-retired catalog product that lists the disease gives its own series for the disease, else the disease's generic series, else every series; a retired product, `free`, `none` or a product that does not list the disease gives every series (Q36). Implied doses make every series a candidate (Q30). The candidates are the union over the records. With no dose given: every series minus those of retired products, or every series when none is left (Q38). `seriesUsed` lists the candidates in rule-set order, complete ones included (Q26); it is omitted after a step-1 or step-2 ⚪ and for ⚪ `NO_BIRTH_DATE` with no dose.
- Per candidate, steps 5–7 run as in S1/S2. A `DOSE_INVALID`/`DOSE_POSSIBLY_INVALID` from any candidate is kept (Q31). Every candidate complete → ✅ `COMPLETE`. Otherwise k = the smallest next dose number among the candidates still needing a dose, and only the candidates at k are merged: E, Du and O are each the latest over them (EQ6 item 2), one `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS{series}` per candidate at k with alternative plans (Q28), and the bucket is classified once from the merged dates.
- `products`: the non-retired products for dose k, in snapshot order. A product series at k contributes its product; a generic series at k contributes every non-retired product that lists the disease and has no series of its own. Omitted when empty or when there is no `nextDose`.
- `SAFEST_SERIES{candidates}` when two or more candidates remain, each `{product, series}` with `product` omitted for a generic series. `PRODUCT_NOT_IN_CATALOG{doses}` (record IDs by ID) with ✅ `COMPLETE` when some record of the disease has `freeProduct`; it sets `est`. A retired product never gives it (Q29).
- Reason order of one end: 1 `IMPLIED_EARLIER_DOSES`; 2 `SAFEST_SERIES` (doses given, emitted once); 3 `BIRTH_DATE_IMPRECISE`; 4 `SAFEST_SERIES` (no dose given, a bucket reason of each end); 5 per dose in walk order, then by candidate in rule-set order, `DOSE_INVALID`, `DOSE_POSSIBLY_INVALID` or `INTERVAL_UNVERIFIABLE` (de-duplicated); 6 `COMPLETE`; 7 `PRODUCT_NOT_IN_CATALOG`; 8 `PREVIOUS_DOSE_DATE_UNKNOWN`; 9 `NO_BIRTH_DATE`; 10 `FIRST_DOSE_DATE_ASSUMED`; 11 `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS` by series in rule-set order; 12 `ON_TRACK`. Record-scoped reasons (`UNKNOWN_PRODUCT` included) stay alone, sorted by record ID. In a two-end ⚪ the doses-given `SAFEST_SERIES` (item 2, emitted once like `IMPLIED_EARLIER_DOSES`) comes before `BIRTH_DATE_IMPRECISE`, while the no-dose `SAFEST_SERIES` (item 4, one end's reason) comes after it.
- Bucket reasons: `COMPLETE`, `ON_TRACK`, `ALTERNATIVE_PLANS`, and since S3a `PRODUCT_NOT_IN_CATALOG` and, with no dose given, `SAFEST_SERIES`. They describe one end's bucket: under a blocking reason they stay with the masked bucket, and when the ends agree on a result that is not ⚪ they come from the later end only. In S3a neither new one depends on the birth end (the same records, the same candidates), so the two ends always give the same one and no golden can tell "from the later end only" apart from "de-duplicated".
- Merge goldens: on `illustrative-products` one candidate at k is later than or equal to the others on all three dates (for example `pertussis-pertu2` over `pertussis-primary` at dose 2, `rota-rotateq` over `rota-rotarix` at dose 1), so those goldens separate "latest" from the earliest-due candidate but not "each date on its own" from "the whole latest candidate". `minimal-crossed-candidates` pins that (EQ6 item 2), and the order of `products` (snapshot order, not candidate order).
- S4 note (issue #14 In scope 11, "golden dates stay well inside any future max age"): four goldens assess rota with no rota dose after b + 15w = 04-16, the rota start limit of the prototype data: `eq6-latest-dates-across-candidates` and `candidates-disagree-on-minimum` (today 04-20, age 15w4d), `a2-generic-plus-specific` and `alt-plans-under-unknown-product` (today 05-10, age 18w3d). The decided case dates and "each golden lists every disease of its fixture" fix them. S4 keeps them unchanged only by giving both rota series of `illustrative-products` a `maxAgeStart` of 19w or more (b + 19w = 05-14, after 05-10); with a shorter limit S4 re-derives them. Every other S3a golden date is inside the prototype's rota limits (rota doses by 05-01, `rota-rotateq` dose 3 due 07-01, before 32w = 08-13).
- `illustrative-products` (version `illustrative-products-s3a`), birth 2026-01-01 (day) unless stated, so b + 6w = 02-12, b + 2m = 03-01, b + 10w = 03-12, b + 3m = 04-01, b + 4m = 05-01, b + 6m = 07-01. Buffer 0 everywhere, so O = Du + 7d.
  - `rota-rotarix` (product `rotarix`): dose 1 min age 6w at 2m; dose 2 min interval 4w at 4m.
  - `rota-rotateq` (product `rotateq`): dose 1 min age 6w at 10w; dose 2 min interval 4w at 4m; dose 3 min interval 4w at 6m. `rotasiil` lists rota but has no series, and rota has no generic series.
